It is a printed Latin *Liber defunctorum* table, one opening to an image, house numbers but no entry numbers, in Latin to 29 September 1848 and from 1849 in Croatian, going back to Latin in January 1858. **None of the three names stands in it.** Priests called Josephus do occur, with other surnames, and are not the Josephus of the Defranceschi: Dominus Josephus Umiljenović, *parochus pensionatus* (image 19, 11 August 1830), and Josephus Mažuranić, a capitular priest who supplies in entry 28 of 3 June 1844 (image 62); a burial note of 19 December 1840 («per H…[illegible] Josephi Cooperatorem», image 54 left) may name a cooperator Josephus and is not settled. The buriers are otherwise the chapter and its chaplains; the lay Josephi of the parish and the schoolmaster Dominus Josephus (Wonzhina / Wonthkino, 1825 and 1839) are not priests.

**What this nil says about the Kalanj of Novi.** The Kalanj of Klenovica who baptise their children at Novi from 1893 (Martin Kalanj, son of Josip, and Marija, born Peričić, told above), and **Josip and Rosalia Perković** of Klenovica house 22, and Ana Kalanj and her husband the klesar Josip Defranceschi, are not among the dead of 1823–1859 in this parish, in any role in any cell the readers quoted. A parish nil is worth that and no more: the Kalanj of Klenovica belong to the parish of Ledenice, whose death books have been read separately, and nobody in this run is a Defranceschi or a Kovačina. **Leads that came to nothing:** a mother or widow born *Peričić* in several entries (for example 6 March 1835) and *Perković / Ferković* as surnames of Novi (image 87, 25 August 1849, a Jure son of Josip Ferković «iz Ledenic», aged 8): not Rosalia and not her family on anything the cells say. Place only: Ledenice (images 13, 6 October 1827; 87; 118 right, 28 January 1858, Filippus Cvitković «e Ledenicensi Parochia oriundus»; 115 left, 8 March 1857, Vid Butković «iz Sela povile, plovanie Ledeničkoga»).

**Zoomed by me, and not Kalanj.** *Image 64, right page (p. 173), entry 85, 13 December 1844, house 278* (levels 13 on the whole upper right page, then on the cell): «Maria filia Joannis Piškulić & Maria nata [one struck word] / Kalj», aged 3, *tussis convulsa*. The mother's maiden name is **«Kalj»** after a struck-out word, and I could not settle it further: it is not a catalogued Kalanj form (not Kalanj, Kalain, Kallayn or any of the forms seen on the Kalanj's own records), the scribe has struck a first attempt and written the name over again, and the Novi families of that surname-shape are Kukalj (house 324–326 in the same years: images 62, 63 and 65 here). I have **not** added it to the Atlas and have **not** counted it. *Image 104, right page (p. 251), 4 September 1854*: «Kate kći suprugah Andrija i Mare Su- / Kalj», half a year old, *lijavica* (level 12, the whole page): a name broken across two lines, **Su-kalj / Ku-kalj**, not Kalanj. *Image 109 left, 19 August 1855*, «Mare rođene Ku-/Kalj» (a reader, not zoomed) is the same line-break trap, read as Kukalj.

**Places, as the readers found them (not counted).** *Bakar*: image 59 right, 7 April 1843, Philippus Mudrović died and was buried there «at his canon brother's» («Buccari»); images 36 (1836) and 62 (14 July 1844, «Obiit … Buccari, & ibi sepultus»); image 114 left, 13 August 1856, a child whose parents are «iz Bakarske Drage» (Bakar's Draga). *Kraljevica* («Portus Regius»): image 47 left, 21 August 1838, a soldier of the Ogulin Regiment who died on the way there; image 57 right, 22 June 1842, the Kraljevica cemetery; image 92 right, July 1850, a soldier «hodeći iz Kraljevica». *Bribir*: 1832, 22 July 1836 (image 38 right), image 120 right, 21 December 1858, Joannes Kersul(?) of Bribir found dead on the road between Novi and Bribir. *Klenovica*: image 16, 6 August 1829. *Senj*: 14 August 1836 and 2 August 1838. *Rijeka*: image 107 left, 7 July 1855, a man who died «u gradskoj bolnici u Reci». Also Karlobag (1836, 1849), Grobnik (image 36), Trieste (24 July 1855), Cilli («u Zagorju kod Cilli», 16 October 1848). No Draga proper, Trsat, Fiume as a parish or Crikvenica in a way that bears on a name.

**Near-names, none of them counted.** *Kobalin / Kaballin / Kabalin* in very many entries from 1823 to 1859 (the nearest to the eye, and always K-o/a-b-a-l-l-i-n); *Kukalj* from 1827 to 1858 (images 38 right and 40 left, July 1836, «Lucia uxor Bartholomei Ku-/kalj», house 326; 44, 46, 52, 53, 54, 58, 59, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 72; Bartholomeus Kukalj, 71, 29 September 1846, image 67, zoomed by a reader at the line break); *Kargačin / Karzacin* in very many, among them the canon Agricola Karzacin (image 118 left, 18 January 1858) and the Lieutenant Joannes Kargacin of the 1809 insurrection (image 119 left, 19 June 1858); *Piskulić / Piškulić* (many); *Toljan* (the cooperator Joannes Toljan, died 2 October 1827); *Vončina / Wonzhina*; *Umiljenović* (Dominus Josephus Umiljenović, parochus pensionatus, image 19, 11 August 1830, a priest of that name and not Josephus Defranceschi); *Caballini* (A.R.D. Joannes-Nicolaus Caballini, 1823, image 5); *Hoballini* (image 6, p. 60, 30 September 1823, first letter H/K/Z not settled, K-o-b-a-l-l-i-n in form). *«Franciscus Ču-kulić(?)», parochus pensionatus* (image 21, p. 91, 20 June 1831) is a different name. *Franciscus* occurs as a given name and a patronymic only. **Not read, and so not a nil:** every cell the readers read at crop magnification only, which is every cell except the three above (no reader could zoom); the first letter of the *Hoballini* cell on image 6 and of the cells «Makabunich» (p. 105, 18 January 1833), «Drickia / Vrichia» (16 December 1833) and «Navor / Lavor» (19 August 1835); the Piran ship and the surname «Zhoranich?» (image 57 left, 15 December 1841); **image 54 left, 19 December 1840, a burial note «per H…[illegible] Josephi Cooperatorem»**, which may name a cooperator Josephus and was not zoomed; the order of image 50, an exact duplicate exposure of 49; the pair of images 89 and 90, which carry the same dates and pages (222–223, 6 September to 4 October 1849) and are very probably one opening photographed twice (a weak image hash, not settled); the **gap of about 13 November to 16 December 1847** (images 69–70, no entries, with the book changing hand to Adalbertus Mariassevich at that point) and the **gap of December 1857 and 1–8 January 1858** (image 117 right, folio 139, blank after 29 November; the Latin series begins on 9 January); the year-turn rows and the month marks 8bris/9bris on pp. 136–137.

sections.lab: Hreljin 1800–1844: baptisms, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: No Kalanj, no Kovačina and no Defranceschi in the Hreljin baptisms of 1800–1844
paras: **8 November 2026.** The Hreljin baptism books on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R2F-4WT, Croatian State Archives, Rijeka, roll 40, 290 images) hold two books. **Item 3** (the roll's slate and the card inside the cover read *Matična knjiga rođenih 1772–1815*) is a hand-ruled Latin register, one entry to a paragraph with the hamlet and house number in the left margin (Poljice, Zlobin, Zastene, Melnice, Vlaka, Ruxich and others); the readers found the first baptism on **image 24, right page (page 1), July 1800**, and the last on **image 91, 14 October 1815**; before it stand a leader and slates (images 0–5, with an inventory of the collegiate church of 1752) and the church's own loan and account ledgers of 1732–1779 in Italian, Croatian and Latin (images 6–23), which are not baptisms. **Item 4** (*Liber baptizatorum in ecclesia S. Georgii M. in Hrelin*, a Latin printed table from the Rijeka press of Karletzky, 1815; the archive card reads *1815–1844*) begins on **image 97 with the tail of 1815 (23 November)** and runs, one opening to an image, to **image 280, entry 112 of 31 December 1844, «Finis. Sequitur Annus 1845»**; image 281 is two blank ruled pages; images 282–287 are a note of 1822 on the blessing of bells at Novi Vinodolski, two house registers of Novi, the end-of-item card, the slate of item 4 and a card saying the book **continues on roll 41**; 288 is the end-of-roll slate and 289 a blank frame. Between the two books come a cover (images 92–96, with 94 a repeat of 93). Every image from 0 to 289 was looked at once by readers who quoted every cell that could be a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role (the child, the parents, the godparents, the baptising priest, the margin). **None of the three names stands in it.** The baptisers are the parish priest Mathias Ballaffy (Ballaff, Ballas) and a succession of cooperators (Antonius Kukuljan, Dominicus Grego, Joannes Soichy, Paulus Prauditza, Stephanus Stanich, Ignatius Bontich and others). Priests called Josephus occur, with other surnames: **Josephus Pipinich**, cooperator, who baptises on image 234 right, 16 November 1839, entry 95, and a visiting Franciscan, **Josephus Calasantius**, on image 230 left, April 1839; neither is the Josephus Defranceschi of Draga; a «R.D. Josephus Bondich» is godfather on image 273 right, 18 February 1844 (entry 20), a lay or unsettled role, not a baptiser.

**What this nil says about the Kalanj and the Defranceschi.** Hreljin is a different parish from Ledenice, Bribir, Draga and Novi, and none of Josip and Rosalia Kalanj of Klenovica, Ana Kalanj, Martin Kalanj or the klesar Josip Defranceschi, nor a Kovačina, stands in any cell the readers quoted. A parish nil is worth that and no more. **The one place that matters is Draga, and it is a sponsor, not a family.** I zoomed it at level 13: *image 155, left page (p. 116), entry 74, 14 December 1829*, «A.R.D. Antonius Mudrovcich Presbyter … baptizavit infantem die 13a natum ex legitimis conjugibus Jacobo et Hellena Blaxina … nomen Lucia. Patrini fuere Martinus et Hellena Stepcovich Parochiae Dragensis» (godparents of Draga; the child's own parents are of Hreljin; no target name). A second Draga sponsor stands on *image 248 right, entry 63, 21 July 1841* («Paschalis uxor Ignatii Marczan ex Parochia Dragensi», read by a reader) and a third on *image 211 left, entry 60, 28 July 1837* («Michael Smokvina ex Parochia Dragensi», read and zoomed by a reader; Smokvina is a near-name only). **Bakar** (*Parochia Buccarensis*) stands very often as a sponsor's home, and the woman «Antonia Zuvicich / Zuvich / Zuditsch» of Bakar is godmother again and again from 1838 to 1844 (images 219, 222–225, 237, 248, 250, 260, 266, 267, 279, 280); others are Domicella Clementina Voich (image 190 right, 8 October 1835), Joannes Ballaff, the Bakar school's catechist (image 230 right, 6 May 1839), «Martino Thian … Parochiae Buccarensis degentibus in Lepenice» (image 252 right, entry 116, 8 November 1841), and in 1844 the Bakar chapter's supply priest and Ballaffy's own title *Pro-Archidiaconus Buccarani Districtus* (image 276 left, entry 54; 279 right, entry 98). **Fiume** (Rijeka) stands as a government town and a parish («ex Parochia Fluminensi», image 271 left, entry 99, about 17 November 1843, Hellena Susan): image 171 right, entry 32, 1 May 1833 (the Gubernium, a godfather's wife); image 183 right, entry 76, 1 October 1834 (the capitular supply priest Vincentius Stiglich of Rijeka baptises); image 249 right, entry 77, 19 August 1841 (Paulina daughter of the late Philippus Mikich «ex Parochia Fluminensi»); image 258 right, entry 40, 10 July 1842 (a concipist at the Gubernium); and, unsettled, image 142 right, entry 7, 21 January 1828 («Barbara Sverjuga Filia Fiumensis?») and image 161 left, entry 4, 4 January 1831. Kraljevica (*Portus Regius*, Portoré), Kastav, Praputnik and Novi also occur as places. No Trsat; image 158 left, entry 42, 27 August 1830, has an unsettled «Tercerno?».

**Zoomed by me, and not Kalanj.** *Image 173, right page (p. 153), 8 and 11 August 1833* (level 13): the baptiser is *Antonius Kukuljan Cooperator*, and the second entry names the mother «Margaritha nata **Kukalj** huius Parochiae», wife of Michael Kucsan: Kukalj, not Kalanj. The name stands in the same hand as the cooperator's own surname, so the cell is settled. *Image 155 left*, above, is Draga and settled. Everything else rests on the readers' words at crop resolution, because no reader could zoom.

**Near-names, none of them counted.** *Kanjer / Kanjar* (a father or godfather «Mathias Gregorii Kanjer», 31 January 1808, image 62 right; 30 January 1838, image 219 right, entry 9; 1839, entries 16, 53 and 64; 1840, images 236 and 237), never with an l; *Frankulin / Frankholin* (1839–1840, images 230 right, 235 left, 238 right, 242 left); *Franovich / Francovich / Franciscevich / Francisovich* (images 229 left, 236 left, 241 right) and *Franjer(?)* (image 257 right, entry 32); *Kalafatich* (image 255 right, entry 4, 10 January 1842); *Kalesasich / Kalefasich* (image 160 right, about 25 December 1830); *Kukalj / Kukuljan* (1833 as above, and the priest Antonius Kukuljan, 1831–1833); *Georgio Rukavina / Bukavina* (image 240 left, entry 59, 3 August 1840, a zoomed reading); *Demelli* (image 242 right). A single reader «Franki(?)» as the priest's name on image 41 left, 20 November 1803, and «Stellano Fran…» in the loan ledger on image 14 left (1752) were not zoomed and are not told as anything.

**Not read, and so not a nil:** every cell read at crop magnification only (all but the two cells above); the front matter (images 3–23) which carries church accounts and not baptisms and which several readers could only read in part (images 6, 7, 9 and 10 have show-through); the first baptism of the roll is page 1 on image 24 right in **July 1800**, so the 28 years the slate promises, **1772 to June 1800, are not in this book on this roll** (no baptisms stand on any page before image 24; the leaves may be lost, not filmed, or the slate may reach back to the book's first ledgers); the **five weeks between the books**, 15 October to 22 November 1815 (image 91 ends on 14 October 1815, image 97 begins on 23 November); the interval of 30 June to 7 August 1812 in item 3, which may be a lull and not a gap; entry 61 absent in 1825, 41 skipped in 1829 (page 110), two numbers (75 and 92) used twice in 1826, the unnumbered entry of 4 March 1827, and the header «Baptizavit Obstetrix» of entry 6 in 1830, all as the readers found them, not settled; the duplicate exposure of image 94 on 93 and an overlay torn from the left of image 284; the faint show-through on 284; the doubtful or unsettled place words named above. The book **continues on roll 41 from January 1845**, which has not been opened.

sections.lab: Hreljin 1845–1857: baptisms, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: Antonia, daughter of Mihovil Kalanj of the Ledenice parish, is the mother of a baby baptised at Hreljin in 1851
paras: **8 November 2026.** The Hreljin baptism book that follows the one told above (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2X-YWY, Croatian State Archives, Rijeka, roll 41, 79 images; the slate reads *Župa Hreljin, matična knjiga rođenih 1845–1857, item 1*) has a Kalanj in it. **Image 32, right page, entry 25 of 1851, 13 May 1851** (zoomed by me, the whole page at level 12 and the entry at level 13), in the Croatian of the parish priest Anton Mudrovčić: «*Godine 1851 dana 13 svibnja ja Anton Mudrovčić župnik krstih sina Franje **Barića** Tomina, rodom iz Gospića u C.Kr. regimenti Ličkoj, i njegove žene Antonia kćere Mihovila **Kalanja** iz župe Ledeničke u C.Kr. regimenti Ogulinskoj. Komu bi ime Josip dano. Kumi biahu Gosp. Juraj Kružić, namjestni šumesetnik na Medji kod S. Josipa, i Marija žena Gosp. Josipa Polića odsadašnjeg trgovca*»: the child is **Josip**, the father **Franjo Barić, son of Toma, of Gospić in the Lika regiment**, the mother **Antonia, daughter of Mihovil Kalanj of the parish of Ledenice in the Ogulin regiment**; the godparents are Juraj Kružić, an official on the Medja near St Joseph's (the word reads «šumesetnik»), and the wife of a merchant. *doc* for every word. **Kalanja** is the genitive of Kalanj («daughter of Mihovil Kalanj»), a case ending and not a spelling, so nothing is added to the Atlas catalogue; the form Kalanj is already in it. The entry does not give the father's trade in the lines I read.

**What it settles and what it does not.** *Settled (doc):* in 1851 a Franjo Barić of Gospić and an Antonia Kalanj, whose father Mihovil Kalanj is of the parish of Ledenice, are husband and wife and have a legitimate son Josip at Hreljin. *Inferred:* that this is **the couple of Bakar**, told above: a Franciscus Barić and an Antonia Kallanj with an unmarried child at Bakar on 20 April 1842, a finance supervisor Franciscus Barić and a wife written Anna ?alanj on 24 December 1855, and a Franciscus Barić, finance pensioner, with Antonia Kalanj at Krasica on 25 March 1857. The Christian names and the mother's surname agree in all four places, a marriage between 1842 and 1851 would turn the illegitimate child of 1842 into a legitimate one of 1851,; the 1851 entry carries no trade for Franjo and no place that makes it Bakar. It is **inf**, and no entry says it. *Not settled:* who Mihovil Kalanj was. The Ledenice births above hold a **Michael and Margarita Kalayn** with children baptised in 1819–24, and a Michael is the Latin of Mihovil; whether Antonia is one of those children is not said by any entry I have quoted, and is a lead, not a finding. Nor does it say that Mihovil's family and Anna's, of Klenovica, are kin: both are Kalanj of the Ledenice parish, and that is all the page shows. **A correction:** the paragraphs on Bakar above said her parents were not named; they are named here, and the two sentences are changed to say so.

**The rest of the volume, a nil.** Waypoint 9R2X-YWY holds **images 0–5**, slates, a blank and resolution charts (roll 41, filmed 8 November 1996, «nastavak» of roll 39, the slate of item 1); **image 6**, the cover; **images 7–59**, the baptisms from **3 January 1845 (page 1, image 7 right) to 31 December 1857 (image 59)**, hand-ruled, in Latin to the middle of 1848 and in Croatian from then on (numbering restarts each year; Anton Mudrovčić, parish priest, and his cooperators; Ballaffy is *Pro-Archidiaconus Buccarani Districtus* in 1845–46); **image 60**, a closing note of 31 December 1857 with a blank right page; **images 61–77**, **confirmation registers** (29 June 1859 at Portorè, entries 1–263; then from 17 September 1863, Bishop Soić, entries 1–287 in Latin and 1–190 in Croatian); **image 78**, the end slate. **No baptisms of 1858 to 1863 stand in this volume**: they are in the next one, waypoint 9R2X-YWR, which has not been opened. Every image from 0 to 78 was looked at once by readers who quoted every cell that could be a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role. **No Defranceschi and no Kovačina stands in it, no priest called Josephus, and no other Kalanj or Barić.**

**Places, as read (not counted).** *Draga*: image 10 left, entry 50, 3 July 1845, «Antonius Stipkovich Mercator ex Parochia Drazensi» (a godfather; a reader checked it at zoom; a Stipkovich *alias* Kulanich / Kallanich stood at Draga in 1727, told above, and nothing here joins them); image 34 left, entry 60, 12 September 1851, «Pashva žena Vatroslava Marcana iz Drazke (Draške) župe»; and an uncertain «Dragensis» godmother in the confirmations of 1863 (image 73, entries 372 and 395). *Bakar*: very often as a sponsor's home, most of all Antonia Zuvicich (1845–47), and in 1850 a police sergeant «u Bakru» (image 30 left, entry 27); in 1851 «iz župe Bakarske» (images 33 right, 34 left); in 1855–57 a few more (images 49, 50, 57). *Trsat*: image 20 right, entry 31, 2 May 1847, «Theresia uxor Bellen ex Parochia Tersactensi». *Fiume / Rijeka*: image 24 left, entry 18, 23 March 1848, «Elisabetha Vidua defuncti Blasii Milissich Flumineensis»; image 38 left, entry 83, 7 November 1852, «župljeni Riečke»; image 39 right, entry 20, 23 March 1853, a mother «iz Rěke». Also Kraljevica (Portorè), Gospić, Ogulin, Karlobag, Novi.

**Near-names, none of them counted.** *Kanjer / Kanjar / Kanja / Kanjn* (1848, 1849, 1851, 1853, 1855–56, and in the confirmations of 1859 and 1863: never with an l; image 65 right, entry 176, was zoomed by a reader and has no l); *Kukalj* (a mother, 1859 confirmations); *Kalafatić / Kalafat* (godfather Petar Kalafatić, 18 April 1857, image 55 right, entry 21; Victoria Kalafat, image 66 right); *Kalvic / Kahlic* (confirmations); *Frankulin*, *Franiskovic / Franceskovic / Franxovich* (a mother Ursula, 1853–57; Ursula nata Franxovich, 16 December 1846, image 18 left, entry 90, not zoomed); *Kovač / Kovačević / Kovačić* (Anton Sirola Kovač, godfather, 1851 and 1853; Karolina Kovačević «iz župe Bakarske», 27 August 1855; Franciscus Kovacich, financial guard, 1846; Kovačić, 1859), *Smokvina*, *Fian*, *Kaniolić / Karolić*. **Not read, and so not a nil:** every cell read at crop magnification only (all but the cell of 1851 and the places a reader zoomed); image 41, a repeat of image 40; the cancelled repeat of entry 95 of 1845 on image 12; the missing entry 18 of 1845, entry 58 skipped and entry 13 written twice in 1847, the unnumbered entries of 17 October 1847 (image 22), 23 April 1849 (image 27 left, with a later note of 1897 under entry 69, image 25 right) and 2 June 1851; the 1874 foot-note correcting entry 66 of 1855 (image 49 right); the doubtful place words named above; and **the baptisms of 1858–1863**, which are in the next volume.

sections.lab: Hreljin 1858–1892: baptisms, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: No Kalanj, no Kovačina and no Defranceschi in the Hreljin baptisms of 1858–1892
paras: **8 November 2026.** The last Hreljin baptism book on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R2X-YWR, *Matična knjiga rođenih 1858–1892*, Croatian State Archives, Rijeka, roll 41, item 2, 424 images) is a single printed Latin table of the Austrian form (Numerus currens; Annus, Mensis, Dies: nativitatis, collati baptismatis; Baptisati; Parentes; Locus domicilii et numerus domalis; Patrinorum; Baptisantis; Observationes), one image to an opening, the left half carrying the child and parents and the right half the house, sponsors, baptiser and remarks. Images 0–4 are slates, a cover (the archive's label *275 (K4) 175*), a pastedown, an endpaper and a faint handwritten preface of 1857; **the first baptisms stand on image 5, 1 January 1858**, and the register runs, with the numbering starting again at 1 each January, to **entry 113 of 21 December 1892 on image 422**, followed by a closing note, the priest's signature and a bare heading «1893.»; image 423 is the end slate. Every image from 0 to 423 was looked at once by readers who quoted every cell that could be a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role (the child, the parents, the sponsors, the baptising priest, the remarks column). **None of the three names stands in it.** There is no Barić with a Kalanj mother either (Barić stands once, as a woman's maiden name in a remark of image 372, not with a Kalanj). The baptisers are the parish priest Antonius Mudrovčić and his successors Ivan Kopanj / Mrkanj, with a run of cooperators (Matthaeus Sablić 1858, Franciscus Vlah 1860s, Joannes Lenac 1870, Fridericus Turk 1872, Sgombić 1873, Martinčić, Bajan and Habek 1875, Karlo Kokalj 1891–92, Dragutin Marušić 1892). **A priest called Josephus occurs once, Josephus Strižić, cooperator, who baptises on image 250 right, entries 38 and 40, April 1876; he is not a Defranceschi.** The entries are in Latin to 1877 and in Croatian by 1878 (image 276); the printed headings stay Latin.

**What this nil says about the Kalanj and the Defranceschi.** Hreljin is a different parish from Ledenice, Bribir, Draga and Novi, and none of Josip and Rosalia Kalanj of Klenovica, Ana Kalanj, Martin Kalanj or the klesar Josip Defranceschi, nor a Kovačina, stands in any cell the readers quoted, in the years in which the Hreljin families of Bakar and Draga were baptising. A parish nil is worth that and no more. **The places that matter come only as a sponsor's home or as a later note, never as a family.** *Draga* is named in the sponsors' cells at image 47 right (entry 16, 1 April 1862), image 53 right (entry 76, 8 November 1862, read by a reader as «ex Parochia Dragen[si]»), image 62 right (entry 50, 3 September 1863), image 73 right (entry 36, 19 April 1864), image 77 right (entry 77, 11 September 1864) and image 97 right (entry 109, 27 November 1865; the word is cut at the line), and, in Croatian, at image 300 right (entry 91, 14 November 1880, «Mate Smokvina iz Draga») and image 341 right (entry 9, 2 February 1885, «u Dragi»); in later notes of the remarks column at image 59 right (entry 34: a marriage «u Dragi» 24 November 1928), image 121 right (entry 69, a death «u Dragi (Sušak)» 1946) and image 354 (a marriage «u Dragi» 13 September 1923). *Bakar* (*Parochia Buccarensis*) is a sponsor's home at image 43 right (entry 97, 31 October 1861), image 58 right (entry 22, 16 April 1863), images 90–91 (1865), image 132 right (entry 46, 2 July 1868), image 163 right (entries 61–62, 21–22 June 1870), image 205 left (entry 134, 5 November 1872, the mother of an illegitimate child), images 252–254 (1876), image 264 right (1877), and the *cooperator Buccarensis* baptises throughout 1875–77 (Martinčić, Bajan or Bujan, Habek, Strižić); later notes name Bakar from the 1910s to 1970 (images 94, 152, 300, 312, 318, 336, 348, 372, 396). *Trsat* (*Parochiani Tersactenses*) is a sponsors' home once, at image 134 right (entry 59, 1 August 1868), and a place of marriage in many later notes (images 51, 90, 144, 187, 276, 288, 300–303, 330, 338, 354, 360, 372–377). *Fiume* is a sponsor's home at image 139 right (entry 97, 18 November 1868, «Fluminensis»), a sponsor row naming «Fluminensem» at image 176 right (entry 23, March 1871; sections.lab: Hreljin 1772–1800: baptisms, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: No Kalanj, no Kovačina and no Defranceschi in the Hreljin baptisms of 1772–1800
paras: **8 November 2026.** The oldest Hreljin baptism book on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R2F-4W5, *Matična knjiga rođenih 1771–1800*, Croatian State Archives, Rijeka, roll 40, item 2, 162 images; the title on the waypoint reads «Births 1771–1800, Baptisms (Krsteni) 1779, 1789, 1796, 1800») is the book whose twenty-eight years the later volume on the same roll (9R2F-4WT, from July 1800) did not hold. It is a handwritten Latin register on unruled pages, one paragraph to an entry, with the hamlet and house number in the left margin and the right-hand pages numbered. Images 0–4 are slates, a blank target, the cover (*Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275 (K4) 171*), an archive slip («1772–1800, 154 leaves») and the Latin attestation and title page «Liber Baptizatorum Parochiae Hrelinensis ab anno 1772»; **the first baptisms stand on image 5, the right page (page 2) opening on 6 January 1772**, the left page carrying four entries headed 1771 or 1773 by the readers' reading; the baptisms run **to image 145, 24 June 1800**, a few weeks before the next volume begins. Images 145 right to 158 are not baptisms but confirmation and sponsor lists, in Croatian under Latin headings (6 June 1789, 27 July 1796, 1800), image 159 is blank, image 160 is the letter of Bishop Caballini for the jubilee of 1776 (Novi Vinodolski, 30 March 1776) and image 161 is the end-of-item slate (roll 40) and the title slate of item 2. Every image from 0 to 161 was looked at once by readers who quoted every cell that could be a Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role (the child, the parents, the godparents, the baptising priest). **None of the three names stands in it, and no priest called Josephus Defranceschi.** The baptisers are the parish priests Georgius Jurichich (Junicich), Martinus Puskarich (from 12 November 1780) and Carolus Cuskarich, the canons Georgius Joannes Puskarich and Thomas Stanislaus Stiglich, and a succession of cooperators and chaplains (Lucas Junicich, Petrus Matteijcsich, Mathias Millos, Mathias Jurich, Bernardus Illijich, Mathias Pauletich, Hieronymus Miladi, Ioannes Kruvich, and a «Georgius Francich, curatus» in 1781–83 and 1789). **One priest called Josephus occurs: «Josephus Cobed(?) Curatus», who baptises on image 105 left in October 1790 (21 and 27 October); I zoomed it at level 13, and the surname begins C-o-b, so he is not a Defranceschi.**

**What this nil says about the Kalanj and the Defranceschi.** The book was read for a Kalayn, a Kalanj or a Barić of the generation before the Kalanj baptisms known from Ledenice and Bakar: **no Kalanj, Kalayn, Callein or Kalagnia stands in any cell the readers quoted**, and no De Franceschi, Franceschi or Kovačina. A parish nil is worth that and no more. *Bakar* (*Parochia Buccarensis*, *Buccarica*) stands as a godparent's home and as the baptiser's office: the chapel of S. Petri of Bakar harbour (image 7 right, image 14 right 17 February 1775, image 35 left 22 January and 10 February 1780), the chaplain Lucas Junicich of Bakar (image 15 left), «Candelaro Buccarensis» (image 22 right, 9 July 1777, zoomed by a reader), «ex ditione Buccaron(sis)» (image 33 left, August 1779), Michael Borchich «ex Parochia Buccarensi» (image 42 right, July 1781), «Mathiae Lever ex Buccarisa» (image 57 right, 27 December 1783), «ex Commertiali Buccrensi» (image 68 left, 21 February 1785) and, zoomed and settled by a reader, Gregorio Iackoncsich Buccarensi (image 129 right, 24 April 1796). *Fiume* stands in a few sponsors' cells («fluminensi», image 20 left; 13 May 1782; image 55 left, 28 July 1783, and right, 22 September 1783; image 59 right, 9 June 1784; and, zoomed by a reader, «Catharina Serich Fluminensi», image 129 right, 24 April 1796). *Kraljevica* (*Portus Regius*, the chapel of S. Nicolai) and *Drivenik* (its parish priests and a canon baptise Hreljin children) recur many times from 1774; Novigrad, Kastav, Kostrena, Trieste and Segni once or twice each. **No Draga and no Trsat, and no Rijeka except the archive's own name.** Image 26 left, in the undated Oct–Dec entries, has a baptism in the chapel at Kraljevica with a godfather «ex Regione Neapolitana», and image 11 right (January 1774) a Ragusan mariner as godfather; neither is a target.

**Zoomed by me at level 13, and not Kalanj.** *Image 64, right page (page 61), the entry of «8vo 9bris» (about 8 November 1784):* Martinus Nicolaus, son of Michael and Margarita, «conthoralium … [Fran]-/…alin», baptised by Petrus Matteijcsich, cooperator, godparents Georgius … -na and Catharina Pasqvan Luce. The reader's «Kalim / Kalin» is the tail of a surname split across the line, and a faint «Fran» stands at the end of the line above; it ends in -lin, not -lanj, and I tell it as Fran-/…lin, the Frankulin family of the book (inf), not Kalanj. *Image 105, left page, 27 October 1790:* «Baptiz: Josephus Cobed Curatus», the priest above. *Image 41, right page (page 39), 21 April 1781:* «Georgium filium Josephi et Mathiae conthoralium K…», baptised by R. Georgius Franicich curatus, godparents Antonio Arglin and Anna Bubanij: the surname is underlined and runs off the trimmed edge of the leaf after its first letter K, so it is **unsettled and not excluded**; the same hand writes «Kagnier» in the entry of 30 April, two entries below (inf, not told as the reading). *Image 10, left page, last entries, February (1773 by the page order, the year not written beside it):* «Matthaeum filium Joannis et Antonia jugalium **Fra?diesa** baptizavit Canus Thomas Stanislaus Stiglich», godparents Stephanus Stanislaus Stiglich and Catharina Tolak(?) Antonij; the underlined surname reads Fra-v/n-d-i-e-s-a, with no c and no h, so I do not read it as a Franceschi or Defranceschi form, but the letters are **unsettled and the cell is not excluded**. Everything else rests on the readers' words at crop resolution, because no reader could zoom (some zoomed a cell with their own enlargement and said so).

**Near-names, none of them counted.** *Frankulin / Franculin / Frankulich / Frankolin* (a Hreljin family on about twenty pages from image 8 to 158, among them images 14 left, 16 left, 26 right, 32 left, 56 right, 74 left, 89 right, 104 left, 119 right, 126 left and the confirmation list on 158 left); *Kanjer / Kanyer / Kanijar / Kagnier / Kagnich* (images 11 left, 16 right, 41 left, 47 left, 57 right, 105 and 106 left, 155 right, 156 and 158; zoomed at 47 left, 105, 106 and 155 by readers, **no l**); *Carina / Corina / Karina / Torina* (many); *Kovacich / Kovacsich / Kovacz* (a sponsor at image 22 right, 2 July 1777; «Kruzich alias Kovacich», image 34 left, November 1779; Joanne Kovacsich, image 35 right, 8 May 1780; «Lovasich / Kovacich», image 38 left, 23 September 1780; images 68 left, 101 right) and the village label «Kovacich» (images 89 left, 90 left), **none Kovačina**; *Kallabotta / Hallabotta* (image 57 right, a sponsor, 10 January 1784, not zoomed); *Kalstich / Halstich* (image 148 left, a confirmation list); *Kolojsfarich* (image 60 left); *Francich / Franicich / Franchich* (the curatus Georgius, 1781–83 and 1789, images 41, 48–53, 96–99, and Franciskovich on 145 right); *Franceschina / Francischina* (a baby's given name, images 33 right, 46 right, 67 right, 68 left); *Mathias Kraglich* (image 110 left). A reader's «Josephus Robar / Pobar / Kobar curatus» of October 1790 is the Cobed above.

**Not read, and so not a nil:** every cell read at crop magnification only (all but the four zoomed above); the **confirmation and sponsor lists of images 145 right to 158**, dense Croatian columns read at about 1400 px and not line by line, which hold the names of many Hreljin families of 1789, 1796 and 1800 and are not a baptism register; the pages whose leaves the readers called out of date order or partly damaged (images 7 left, 12 right and 13 left, 24 to 26 left, 35 right, 63 and 64, 101 right) and the years the readers could not fix (image 24 right, image 26 left); a possible gap of May to July 1779 between images 32 and 33 and of 3 to 24 August 1786 between images 76 and 77; the overlap of two readers' dates at images 89 and 90 (21 January to 4 March 1788 on one, 21 January to December 1788 on the other), not settled; the repeated images (61 repeats 60, 79 repeats 78, 93 repeats 92, 98 repeats 97) and the blank image 71; image 5 right, the last three entries of February and March 1772, written over each other; the blotted or faded cells the readers named (image 38 right, 28–29 October 1780; image 118 right, last entry; image 125 right, a struck entry; images 124 left and 123 left); a few unresolved place words (image 15 right «Ducerensi?», image 112 left, the cooperator Antonius Sojch of «Bucc…/Ruc…ensis?», image 23 right «Buccarich or Buccariensis?»). **This row is a reader pass over every image and not a walk.**

sections.lab: Hreljin 1815–1857: marriages, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: No Kalanj, no Kovačina, no Defranceschi and no Barić × Kalanj marriage in the Hreljin marriages of 1815–1857
paras: **8 November 2026.** The Hreljin marriage book on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R2X-YW1, *Marriages (Vjenčani) 1815–1857*, Croatian State Archives, Rijeka, roll 41, item 3, 90 images; the cover reads *Hreljin vjenčani br. 5*, *Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275 (K4) 176*) is the book in which the marriage of **Franjo Barić of Gospić and Antonia, daughter of Mihovil Kalanj of Ledenice**, would stand if it had been made at Hreljin; the baptism of her son Josip there in May 1851 is the one Kalanj the Hreljin baptisms gave us. **It is not in this book, and neither is any Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role.** Images 0–5 hold no marriage entry (slates, the bishop's Latin authentication of 22 August 1832, a Latin preface of 7 October 1822); image 6 is the cover and an empty leaf; **the first marriages stand on image 7, 19 November 1815**, and the book runs, a printed Austrian table in Latin to 1849 (couples on the left leaf, parents, witnesses and the priest's signature on the right, the entry itself written as one Latin paragraph across the columns) and a Latin form with a Croatian hand from 1850, **to image 84, the last page (page 76), entries 23 to 25 of 25–26 November 1857**, with the Latin closing note signed at Hreljin on 31 December 1857 (the registers closed, new forms from 1 January 1858). Images 85–89 are the end-of-roll slates, a resolution chart and a blank; no index follows the book. Every image from 0 to 89 was looked at by readers who quoted every cell that could be one of the three names in any role (groom, bride, both sets of parents, witnesses, the marrying priest, margin notes): images 6–29, 48–53 and 72–89 once, images 30–47 and 54–71 twice (see the last paragraph). The marrying priests are Puskarich, Merzljak (parish priest and dean), Lucas Blazina and Katnich (1815–26), Praudiza, Mudrovcich and Nicolaus Badia (1827–32), Kukuljan, Ballaf(f)y, Soich and Bontich (1833–46), then Mudrovčić (župnik) and Mate Sablić (kapelan) to 1857. **No priest called Josephus Defranceschi:** the Josephus of the book are the administrator of Kastav «Rdo Dno Josepho Bobar» (image 25 right, 18 June 1827), «Josephus Pobar» the pro-dean (images 36–41, 1833–36; the same man, inf) and a lay witness Josephus Polich, scriba (images 48–53, 1841).

**The Barić pair, and the Barić-like names that are not it.** No Franjo Barić and no Antonia Kalanj stands in the book, and no groom or bride from Gospić or from the Lika regiment. The Hreljin readers met a local family of the Baretich type, **none zoomed and none counted**: «Michael Barctich/Baretich Joannis» (image 7, 1815, row 4, father Joannes Baretich Jacobi), «Mathiae Barotich/Bartulich» (image 31 left, 25 November 1829, a bride's father), «Antonium Gregorii Bara-/sich? Dolensem» (image 34 left, entry 13, 2 June 1831), Tiburtius Baretich (image 48, 1839, entry 29, parents Matthaeus Baretich and Maria Blaxina), «Helena Baretich» (image 56 right, 1 May 1843, entry 9, a bride's mother), Lucas Barebich/Baretich/Baritich of Mali Dol (image 68, 17 November 1847, entry 19, son of Matthaeus, the spelling unsettled) They are Hreljin and Dol men; a Barić of Gospić is not among them. **What this nil says:** the marriage of the Barić and the Kalanj was not made at Hreljin between 1815 and 1857 (inf); the Bakar and Krasica baptisms of 1842–57 and the Hreljin baptism of 1851 name them, and this book adds nothing to where they married.

**Looked at by me, and not Kalanj.** I looked at the 1400-pixel crops of the two cells the readers could not settle; neither is a level-13 zoom. *Image 65 right, entry 28 (25 November 1846, Rochus Pasquan and Juliana Sporar):* the groom's father is Tomas Pasquan and his mother is written «Margarita nata Fran- / kulin», with the line break after Fran, and a witness of the same row is «Georgius Frankulin»; it is the Frankulin family of the book, not Kalanj (inf, one crop). *Image 41 left, entry 10 (23 November 1836):* the groom Andreas Polich's mother is «Margaritha Kanjer»; the word reads K-a-n-j-e-r, with no l (one crop). I also looked at the whole of image 40 as a sanity check on what the volume was (a printed Latin table, *Anno 1836*, Mathias Ballaffy parochus, Hreljin). Everything else rests on the readers' words at crop resolution, because no reader could zoom.

**Near-names and places, none of them counted.** *Kanjer / Kranjer / Kanier / Kagner / Kabjer* (a Hreljin family, with no l, as in the baptisms: images 14, 15 and 17 in 1823–24, 20 and 22 in 1825–26, 37, 39, 40 and 41 in 1834–36, 45–47 in 1838–39, 69, 70, 73 and 77 in 1848–53); *Frankulin / Franculin / Franhulin* (many entries from image 12 to image 83); *Kovacevich / Kovasevich* (image 32 right, entry 12, 18 July 1830, Jacobum Konacevich/Kovacevich of Fužine; a witness at 33 left; Jacobus Kovasevich, images 45–46, 1839), *Kalafatich* (image 27 left, 21 November 1827, a groom of Bribir), *Kabalin / Bubalin* (images 38 right, 40 left), *Kulin* (image 65), *Calawersich* (image 23, entry 19), *Franciskovich* (images 13, 35, 39, 42), *Margan* (image 56), *Burić* (images 81–83), the trade «kovač» (image 70, 1848) and the priest Paulus Kaliman of Lukovdol (images 36–41); the bride «Maria Josipa Jurine rođena Franco» (image 77, 1853, entry 10, a widow of 44), not counted. **Places in cells**, as homes of couples and witnesses: Bakar / Buccari (image 30 right, 3 May 1829; 31 right, 17 February 1830; 33 right, 27 January 1831; 39 left, 40 right, 70, and from 1853 «iz župe Bakarske» at images 77, 82 and 83), Fiume (image 19 entry 6, 27 April 1825, a groom of Vienna and a bride Renaldy; images 31 right and 33 right, 27 January 1831), Draga (image 31 right, 29 November 1829), Kraljevica / Portus Regius (many), Kastav, Kukuljanovo, Fužine, Bribir, Grobnik, Carniola, Jelsa and Ragusa (image 22, 1826), Portole in Istria (1848); **no Trsat and no Rijeka as a place of anyone in the marriages**. A place in a cell is a place and nothing more.

**Not read, and so not a nil.** Every cell at crop magnification except the two I looked at; the unsettled cells the readers named (image 13 left, late 1822, Melnice house 14, «Margareta Franc(.)f Furicich» with the surname partly struck; image 42, 1837, entry 6, the bride's place «Buccarin…/Wenjerica»; image 77, 1853, entry 10, the place words after «Franco», and entry 15, «Preput…mik?»; image 84, entries 23 and 24, a groom's surname («Vukonić?») and a soldier line, and the faint signature of entry 25); the dates of entries the readers gave as faint or smudged (image 48, entry 29, late November 1839); **gaps I did not establish**: June to late 1821 between images 11 and 12, and August 1826 to February 1827 between images 23 and 24 (where the reader notes «Sequitur Annus Communis 1827» and a crossed-out page; whether any marriage stood in those months I did not check); the repeats (image 26 repeats 25, 46 repeats 45, 74 repeats 73), image 41 right (ends cancelled by diagonal strokes) and image 71 (rest struck through). **The first readings of images 36–47 and 60–71 were of a different book** (a Bakar marriage register of 1711–1727 left in an old working folder with the same name); they were found out by the readers, discarded and read again from freshly decoded images, so nothing of them is told here. **This row is a reader pass over every image and not a walk.**

sections.lab: Hreljin 1815–1857: deaths, read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: No Kalanj, no Kovačina and no Defranceschi in the Hreljin deaths of 1815–1857
paras: **8 November 2026.** The Hreljin death book on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R2D-GPF, *Matična knjiga umrlih 1816–1857*, Croatian State Archives, Rijeka, roll 42, item 1, 126 images; *Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275 (K4)*, filmed by the Croatian State Archives, Zagreb, 21 November 1996) is the book in which a **Kalanj, a Kovačina or a Defranceschi who died in the parish of Hreljin** would stand, and the third Hreljin book of the period read (the baptisms of 1772–1892 and the marriages of 1815–57 are told above). **None of the three names stands in it in any role** (the deceased, a parent or a spouse named in the entry, an informant, the priest, a margin note), and no Antonia Kalanj, Mihovil Kalanj or Franjo Barić is among the dead. Images 0–5 are slates, a blank frame, two test targets and the roll dividers (the title slate reads «Matična knjiga umrlih 1816–1857, item 1», roll 42); image 6 is the cover, image 7 the flyleaf (the bishop's authentication of 22 August 1836 and a label) and **page 1, the first deaths (1815–16)**; the book is a printed Latin *Liber Defunctorum* (columns for the month, the house number, the name of the dead, the religion, the sex, the age and the cause of death), at first with an entry a line, from about 1827 as running Latin sentences across the columns, and, **from entry 37 of 1848 (9 September 1848), written in Croatian**. It runs **to image 124, the last page**: pages 226–235, entries 3 to 68 of 1857, 13 January to 26 December 1857, with the signed Latin closing note of 31 December 1857 (the old register closed) on the left page of image 124 and a blank right page; **image 125 is the end-of-item slate and the title slate**. Every image from 0 to 125 was looked at by readers who quoted every cell that could be one of the three names. Entries stand on images 7 to 124 in date order (the readers' ranges: images 7–11 pages 1–9 to 9 September 1819; 12–17 pages 10–21 to 17 August 1821; 18–23 pages 22–33 to 5 September 1824; 24–29 pages 34–45 to 16 August 1827; 30–35 pages 46–57 to 4 September 1829; 36–41 pages 58–69 to 23 October 1830; 42–47 pages 70–81 to 18 April 1834; 48–53 pages 82–93 to 31 August 1836; 54–59 pages 94–105 to 17 March 1838; 60–65 pages 106–117 to 22 April 1841; 66–71 folios 118–129 to 13 December 1843; 72–77 pages 130–141 to 11 August 1845; 78–83 pages 142–153 to 9 August 1847; 84–89 pages 154–165 to the first days of 1850; 90–95 pages 166–177 to 1852; 96–101 pages 178–189 to 19 February 1854; 102–107 pages 190–201 to 24 February 1855; 108–113 pages 202–213 to 9 September 1855; 114–119 pages 215–225 to 6 January 1857; 120–125 pages 226–235 and the end slates). The priests are Joannes Merzljak (parish priest and dean, who died on 23 February 1833, entry 11, image 45 right), Leopoldus Franciscus Puskarich, Lucas Blazina, Paulus Praudiza, Mudrovcich, Mathias Ballaf(f)y, Antonius Kukuljan, Joannes Soich, Ignatius Bontich, and from 1845 Anton Mudrovčić (župnik) and Mate Sablić (kapelan). **No priest called Josephus Defranceschi:** the only Josephus of a priest is Josephus Paraž, parish priest of Merkopalj (entry 22 of 1836, images 48–53); the lay Josephus of the book are a Ruxich (1826) and a Marohnich (1827).

**What this nil says.** The Kalanj of Ledenice who give their daughter Antonia to Franjo Barić of Gospić (the Hreljin baptism of 1851, told above) is not among the Hreljin dead of 1815–57, and no Kalanj of any place stands among them (inf). A parish nil is worth that and no more. **The Barić-like names are a Hreljin family and are not counted:** *Baretich / Barettich* (image 9 left, page 4, house 12, August 1818: Blasius, son of Matthias, Anna, his daughter, and Stephanus, her brother, of dysentery on 20, 30 and 31 August; image 20 right, page 27, house 40, 1822: Nicolaus Baretich 69 on 18 July, Maria Lukcsick née Baretich on 6 August and Anna, wife of Nicolaus, on 15 August), *Baresich / Barešić* (image 39 left, entry 55 of 1830, 27 May 1830, a boy of twelve, son of Matthaeus), and *Juraj Barčić* «iz župe Bosiljevacke, sela Herzina» (image 91 left, entry 47 of 1850), who is not a Barić of Gospić. **Zoomed by me at level 13, and not Kalanj:** *image 8, right page (page 3), 10 November 1817, house 45:* «Catharina filia Vincentii Pasquan dicti …», with the interlinear words «Kolaz» above and «…ti Krabuglia» below; the surname word is **Krabuglia** (K-r-a-b-u-g-l-i-a), an alias of the Pasquan family, and not Kalanj; the readers' «Rabughia/Kalughia?» was this word. Everything else rests on the readers' words at crop resolution, because no reader could zoom.

**Near-names, none of them counted.** *Kanjer / Kanjir / Kanjera / Kanier / Kanja / Kanjor* (a Hreljin family, without an l: the Thomas Kanjer family of 1827–36 at images 24–29, 30–35, 42–47 and 48–53, the old Jacobus Kanjer of 1843 at image 70 left and the child Mathias Kanjer at image 71 left, «nata Kanja» at image 84 right (entry 46 of 1847), image 108–113 (entries 36 and 55 of 1855) and image 118 right (entry 33 of 1856), a Mato Kanjer, 81, on 3 January 1850 at image 89 right, and Kanjer in 1854 at images 105 and 106), read at crop level except where the first letter is faint (**unsettled, not excluded:** image 59 left, 5 February 1838, entry 5, «Matthaea uxor Jacobi Kianjer / Kanjer(?)»; image 118 right, entry 38, «Jakova Kanjeve(?)»); *Frankulin / Franculin / Frankulina* (many pages from image 14 to image 124), *Kucan / Kucsan / Kuesan* (very frequent), *Kovac / Kovach* (image 67 right, 23 December 1841; the trade «kovač» in images 108–113 and 120–125; none Kovačina), *Franciskovic* (images 105 left), *Thian*, *Turina*, *Marohnich*, *Kaguer*, *Bakarčić* (images 90–95, 1851, a financial inspector's son), the cooperator *Antonius Kukuljan* and a finance guard *Bonifacius Kukuljan* of Karlobag (image 73 right, entry 27, 10 May 1844). The reader's «Kala-» at image 121 left (22 April 1857, entry 21) is the first name Katarina broken at the line end. *A «Calhnat?… Pasqvan»* in image 20 right (entry 17 of 1822) is read as Catharina. **Places in cells (not counted):** Portore / Kraljevica (the royal hospital, many deaths), Bakar (image 11 right, 7 September 1819, a man drowned «prope Buccariam»; image 84 right, entry 51 of 1847, the Bakar poor hospital; image 103 right, entry 42 of 1854; the district surgeon at Bakar in 1847; the Bakar commission in 1854–55), **Draga** (image 76 left, entry 86 of 1844, house «Bretova Draga in Zlobin», a hamlet of Hreljin and not the parish of Draga; and image 102 right, page 191, entry 27, 29 April 1854, a woman «iz župe Draške», not settled), Fiume (image 115 left, entry 7: a death of 1852 noted in 1855 «u Fiumu u Hervatskoj»), Rijeka (image 92 right, entry 33 of 1851, the orphanage), **Trsat** (page 184, left, entry 20 of 1853, a Polić dying «u bolnici Tersatskoj», with a letter of the «C.K. gospoštija Bakarska» of 7 June 1853), Drivenik, Ledenice, Lokve, Cres, Kastav, Kostrena, Grobnik, Karlstadt, Karlobag, Bakar. A place in a cell is a place and nothing more.

**Not read, and so not a nil.** Every cell at crop magnification except the one above; the unsettled cells (image 59 left, entry 5, and image 118 right, entry 38, the first letters of a Kanjer; image 102 right, entry 27, whether Draga; image 65 right, the later marginal notes numbered 1–10, the first read «Bordo»; the block of deaths notified from other places on image 115 left and the 1854 appendix of eleven deaths outside the parish on page 199 (image 106 right), read at crop level; the place readings «Merko-…» (entry 67 of 1852), «Jestu / Jezu» (image 115 left, entries 3, 6 and 9), «Preput…» ; the doubtful entries at images 78–83 (31 March 1846, entry 10, burial by «Thomam Skalabrini(?) emeritum Parochum Dolensem(?)»; 25 July 1847, entry 23, «parochum Stregnensem(?) Antonium Skedrovecsich(?)»); the two entries numbered 25 in 1844 (entry 31 missing) in images 72–77; and a reader's date of 20 June 1852 for the first entry of image 96, which sits before the 26 June 1852 given for the last entry of image 95 (I did not settle which is the slip). **Gaps I did not establish:** between the last entry of an image and the first of the next I did not compare every entry number (the readers gave numbers and dates that follow one another, with the exceptions above); image 125 is a slate and not a page. **This row is a reader pass over every image and not a walk.**

sections.lab: Trsat baptisms 1815 to September 1860 (Liber V, Liber VI to its end, and the first pages of the 1858 book), read page by page · 8 November 2026
sections.h2: A Barić with a wife «Anne Kalain» at Podvežica on 3 August 1845, and no Kovačina, in the Trsat baptisms of 1815–1860 (read so far)
paras: **8 November 2026.** The Trsat (Tersatto) baptism registers on FamilySearch (waypoint 9R2C-VZH, Croatian State Archives, Rijeka, roll 129, items 3 and 4, 408 images) are being read for the three names in any role (child, parents, godparents, baptiser, margin) and for a priest called Josephus. This is the part read so far, **images 3–143, 150–224 and 232–281, December 1815 to September 1860**: «Liber V Baptizatorum» (Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275 (K4) 537), a printed Latin table «Liber Baptizatorum in Ecclesia» filled with hand-written entries, from the first entries of December 1815 (image 3) to 19 July 1847 (image 143, ending «Sequitur continuatio N. 32 in novo libro»); images 144–147 are the inside back cover, a pasted slip and a loose sea-leave permit, the end-of-item slates and a resolution chart; image 148 is the cover of «Liber VI Baptizatorum» (S. Georgii M., 1847–1857/58, 275 (R4) 538) and **150–224 its pages**, entries 1 of 1847 to the closing line of 31 December 1857 (it ends «Slijedi Knjiga VII od 1858», in hand-ruled boxes, Latin to 1848, Croatian from 13 September 1848, with Latin again from entry 76 of 1857); 225 is a blank leaf with a memorial note of 1856 about the Trsat graveyard, 226–228 are slates and a filming target; 229–231 are the cover and title leaf of the next book, «Matricula Baptisatorum Parochialis Ecclesiae Tersatensis 1858» (Rođeni Trsat 1858–1879, inv. 539, a printed Latin table, one page to an image, five entries to a page), and **232–281 its pages 1–50, 30 December 1857 to 27 September 1860**. **Every image was looked at once by a reader, as a left and a right crop; the volume is not walked and the rest of it (images 282–407, to 1879) is not yet read.** Every cell below that I name as read at level 13 I zoomed myself; the rest stands on the readers' words at crop size.

**The Kalain entry.** **Image 135, right page, page 263 (folio 133), the last entry on the page, 3 August 1845**, house cell «Pod…» (the readers took it for Podvežica, a hamlet of the parish), the first lines zoomed by me at level 13 and the whole entry at level 12: «*Franciscum filium legitimum Francisci **Barich**, et Anne **Kalain** nata jugalium — Levantibus Mathia Marac, et Maria Glavan. Ego Josephus Visner Parochus locali baptizavi in Dno*». The child is Franciscus, the father **Franciscus Barich**, the mother **Anna, born Kalain**, the godparents Mathias Marac and Maria Glavan; the baptiser is the parish priest **Josephus Visner** (a priest called Josephus, and not a Defranceschi; the only other Josephus among the baptisers is a Josephus Scrobogna(?), administrator and parish priest of Grobnik, in 1818 and 1823, whose surname is unsettled). *doc* for every word. **Kalain** is already a form of the Kalanj family in the Atlas catalogue (the two godparents of Bakar in the 1870s, told above), so nothing is added there.

**What it settles and what it does not.** *Settled (doc):* in 1845 a Franciscus Barich and an Anna Kalain are husband and wife and have a legitimate son at Trsat. *Open:* whether this is the couple already told above, a Franciscus **Barić** with an **Antonia** Kallanj at Bakar in 1842, a Franjo Barić of Gospić with **Antonia**, daughter of Mihovil Kalanj of the Ledenice parish, at Hreljin in 1851, and a finance supervisor Franciscus Barić with a wife written **Anna** ?alanj at Bakar on 24 December 1855. The husband's Christian name agrees in all five places and the wife's surname in all five; the wife's Christian name is **Anna** at Trsat in 1845 and at Bakar in 1855 and **Antonia** at Bakar in 1842, Hreljin in 1851 and Krasica in 1857. I do not equate Anna and Antonia, and I do not say that the Trsat Barich is the Gospić Franjo (the entry gives no trade, no origin and no parent): it is *inf* at most that they are one couple, and it may be two. The Trsat entry adds one fixed point, a Barić × Kalain household with a house at Podvežica in the summer of 1845, between the Bakar entry of 1842 and the Hreljin entry of 1851.

**No Kovačina, and no other Kalanj.** In the pages read (1815 to September 1860), no Kovačina form (Kovačina, Kovacina, Kovacsina, Kovatschina, Covacina, Kovachina) and no other Kalanj form (Kalanj, Kallanj, Kalain, Kallayn, Callain, Callajn, Callayn, Callein, Kalagnia, Kalaijn, Kalani, Kalanij, Kalany, Kalayn, Kalianj, Kallaijn, Kallajn, Kallanij, Kallein) stands in any role. **Near-names seen and not counted:** Kovacich (a Hieronymus, 1819 and 1837), Kovanich (1821, the second letter after *Kova-* an n), Covacich, Colazio / Colazic / Kolazio (frequent), Kalafat / Kalafata (a byname, 1849–50), Kukat or Kukal (1822, the last letter l or t at crop size, read as Kukat), Kovac, **Calasantius** (a friar's name, not Kalanj), Smoquina, Smogorina, Smokvina, Margan and the Barić-like Baretich, Baranich, Baraxich, Bacarich; and, in 1850–1860, Kalafat as a caulker's trade or byname (very frequent, always written -fat), Kovač and Kovačić (a coachman, a smith, a joiner, a Saverio Kovačić of Rijeka; always -ić), Kalić and Kalčić, Smokvina, Margan, Bakarčić (Trsat's Bakarčić family, one godmother «iz Drage»), Baretić and Baretta (godmothers, 1858 and 1857), Barbarić, Francović, Frančić, Frankić, Franović, Kobau and «Čašnj». **Unsettled, not excluded (not zoomed):** (1850–1860, at crop size) image 199 left, entry 2 (7 January 1854), a mother «Kranciani» with an uncertain first letter; image 220 right, entries 31 and 33 (1857), «Čašnj», which a reader could also take for «Časnj» or «Kašnj»; image 223 right, entry 86 (31 October 1857), «Kovauč / Kovačić»; image 243 right, entry 63 (1858), a godfather «Nicolò Bari(č)ić / Baucich»; image 249 right, entry 18 (1859), godparents' names blotted («ambo Fluminenses»); image 186 right, entry 27 (1852), an erased sponsor line; (1815–1850, as before, not zoomed) image 24 left, page 42, entry 60 (18 December 1819), a godfather whose name begins «Kanb» or «Kank»; image 87, page 169 (31 August 1834), a «Kak» or «Kalk»; image 91 right, page 177 (4 July 1835), the first entry, a mother «Kall'» or «Rall'»; image 21 right, page 37, entry 28 (10 June 1819), a father's epithet «Lagignia»; image 27 right, page 49, entry 27 (18 June 1820), a father «Franciscus De(f/s)o…t» (a Defranceschi abbreviation, or not). **Places named in cells (not counted):** Draga (the house cell, 1819, 1824, 1830, 1832, 1837, 1849–50; a «mercator Dragensis», 1821), Bakar (godparents, a foundling's mother, 1822, 1844, 1847), Hreljin (a mother «ex parochia Hrelynensi», 1842), Fiume, Susak, Grobnik, Castua; from 1850–1860 Draga (a godparent's origin, 1850–1859, at least a dozen times), Bakar (a mother «rodom iz Bakra», 1850; a godmother «iz Bakra», 1853; a chaplain of Bakar baptising, 1855), Hreljin («ex Parochia Hreljinensi», 1858), Martinščica (a house, 1850–1857). The Defranceschi who stand in this book are told on [the Rijeka page](/rijeka/): sponsors from 1818, a prior of the lazaretto at Martinščica who baptises his children here from 1834, a chancellor of the Health Office at Rijeka, «Franjo Defrančeski», who is godfather at Podvežica on 14 August 1850, and a godmother «Marija Defranci» in 1855 and 1856. **No further Barić × Kalanj baptism, and no Josephus among the priests,** in 1850–September 1860 (the baptisers are the parish priest Paškval Žuvičić and his cooperators Gaspar Matković, Magnus Bošek, Amat Strilčić, Nikomed Žanić and others).

rows_retired.lab: The join: Anna Kalanj, born 3 January 1864
rows_retired.text: Entry 2 of 1864 in the baptismal register of Ledenice, the Vinodol parish above Crikvenica: «Anna, legitima — Josephus Kalanj et Rosalia nata Perković ejus uxor, Brinjensis Parochiæ ruricolæ» — at «Kljenovica N° 22». Godparents Josephus Ban and his wife Anna; baptised by Vincentius Segulja, parish priest. She married Josip Defranceschi, the stonecutter's son who brought this archive's line down from Gračišće to the coast, and she is generation four of the direct line. (doc — the plate is held here.)

rows_retired.lab: ⚠ «Rijenovica» does not exist, and the mistake hid a fact
rows_retired.text: Until today this archive read that place as «Rijenovica house 22» and said so in fifteen files, including the pedigree's own wall note. There is no Rijenovica: the word returns zero hits in this archive's Croatian gazetteer. The register says KLJENOVICA — the older spelling of Klenovica — and the Blažević Archive has read it correctly all along. What the misreading concealed: this site's Crikvenica page already says «House 22 is somewhere in this line of roofs — Anton Rudolf Defranceski was born in it on 20 January 1890.» Anna was born in the SAME HOUSE twenty-six years earlier. The archive held «house 22» at both ends and never joined them. The correction is on /corrections/.

rows_retired.lab: ⚠ And the entry says where they came from: BRINJE
rows_retired.text: «Brinjensis Parochiæ ruricolæ» — country people of the parish of Brinje. No file of this archive carried that phrase, and it is the most important thing in the entry: the Kalanj were not coastal people. Brinje is inland, up behind the Velebit gap, and they had come down to Klenovica on the shore. The Blažević Archive calls Brinje «the single largest hole in this family» and records that «not one page of its register has been opened». So both archives now stand at the same closed door, and this page exists partly to say so.

rows_retired.lab: The oldest open question here is a Kalanj question
rows_retired.text: The registers name ANA KALANJ in all four Crikvenica baptismal entries of her children. The family's own genealogy gives Josip a wife ANA GRUBIŠIĆ, 19 September 1863 – 28 May 1936, and that is the name cut on the Crikvenica gravestone. The registers govern and the stone is unexplained — and the stone no longer exists, because the plot was sold and the monument taken apart, so the photograph of it is now the only record. This is why Anna's page carries no death date: the only date on offer belongs to a name this archive cannot yet reconcile with hers.

rows_retired.lab: The stones — eleven of them, and a sibling set taking shape
rows_retired.text: Eleven Kalanj monuments have now been photographed in the cemeteries of Crikvenica, Novi Vinodolski and Klenovica and are held here as plates. ⚠ AND FOUR OF THEM CLUSTER AROUND ANNA'S OWN GENERATION. LUKA KALANJ 1859–1944 and KATA 1860–1942 on a ledger slab; and ROZALIJA KALANJ 1865–1943, whose first digit is damaged and was read at 5×. Anna was born in 1864. So there are Kalanj born in 1859, 1860, 1864 and 1865 in one small stretch of the Vinodol — and ROZALIJA IS THE NAME OF ANNA'S OWN MOTHER, Rosalia née Perković, which is exactly what a daughter would be called. A sibling set is the obvious reading: Josip Kalanj and Rosalia's children, with the second daughter named for her mother. ⚠ IT IS STILL A GUESS. No stone here names a father, and this archive has spent the day learning what proximity is worth without a document. The test is cheap and specific: THE LEDENICE BAPTISMS OF 1855–1870, where Anna's own entry (number 2 of 1864) already sits, and where her brothers and sisters would sit within a few pages of her. (open, and the most tractable question on this page.) The other stones: Albert 1895–1945 with five of his household; Petar 1913–1971 and Vera 1917–2011 with the infant Milan 1943–1944; Mate 1928–1992; Franjo 1933–2004; a joint Kalanj–Rebrović stone; Vinko 1901–1961 and Paulina 1904–1984; Josip 1950–1983 with Franjo 1909–1991 and Zora 1923–1999; Tomislav 1935–2006; Judita 1934–2012 with Marijan 1931–2019; and Rozalija's own, with Anton 1897–1977, Marija 1898–1989 and Milan 1927–2006. ⚠ And one more, which carries something none of the others do: OBITELJ KALANJ — MARTIN 1905–1988 and MARTINA 1913–1995, two porcelain ovals, a stone cross standing in the gravel above — and propped against the plot, A PINK STONE PLAQUE CUT WITH THE CROATIAN CHEQUY SHIELD, the šahovnica. It is the only national emblem on any stone in this whole set of photographs, and it is worth recording as such and nothing more: a family put it there, and when or why is not on the stone. Two stones could not be stored because they reached this archive inline rather than as files — that one, and LOVRO 1906–1965 with Ana, Ivan and Marijan. They want re-sending if they are to be kept.

rows_retired.lab: Where this page stops, and why
rows_retired.text: The Kalanj genealogy proper — 215 published people, earliest birth 1734, running through Klenovica and Povile — is kept in The Blažević Archive, and is not rebuilt here. That boundary is right, and it had one cost that this page is the answer to: while each archive read only its own page, the two of them held one baptism and disagreed about the village for months. What belongs HERE is the join, the evidence photographed on this side, and the disagreements between the two. What belongs THERE is the family.
